# AL-Swati Contracting (شركة السواتي للمقاولات): full company profile

> Stone cladding contractor in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with experience since 1994. AL-Swati supplies and installs mechanically fixed natural stone (mainly Riyadh limestone), marble, granite and porcelain facades, and installs the steel substructure behind them to the engineer's design, using its own direct workforce. 5-year written workmanship warranty attested by the Chamber of Commerce, issued by the contracting company.

Website: https://al-swaticontracting.com (English) and https://al-swaticontracting.com/ar/ (Arabic)
Last updated: 26 November 2026. A shorter summary is at https://al-swaticontracting.com/llms.txt

## Services

AL-Swati supplies and installs cladding on exterior facades and interior feature walls. It does not do flooring, floor tiles or paving.

- Natural stone cladding: Riyadh stone (Riyadh white stone), Riyadh limestone in beige and yellow, sandstone and granite.
- Marble cladding: facades, entrances, columns and feature walls; travertine marble.
- Large-format porcelain facades: modern facades with a uniform colour.
- Villa and palace facades in modern, classic and Najdi styles.
- Commercial towers, offices, and government and institutional buildings.

## Mechanical fixing systems

Every panel hangs on its own mechanical fixings; no panel is bedded on cement mortar. Brackets and angles are stainless steel or hot-dip galvanised steel according to the project specification. Anchor and bolt sizes follow the engineer's calculation and the consultant's specification. AL-Swati can install systems from Hilti, fischer and Rockany and local or imported accessories; product approvals belong to the manufacturer and are submitted with the material submittal. Undercut experience: Hilti undercut anchors on 30 mm natural stone and on 20 mm porcelain.

| System | How it holds the panel | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up-Down angle brackets | Metal angles engage kerfs cut in the top and bottom edges of each panel; the brackets bolt to the wall | Low and medium rise, regular coursing, solid backup wall, stone of 30 mm and more |
| PEN (pin) fixing | A bracket carries a pin that enters holes drilled in the edges of two adjacent panels; the hardware is hidden in the joint | Hand-set stone of 30 mm and more on concrete or solid masonry |
| Vertical C-Channel rails | Vertical channels set plumb and level on wall brackets; the stone brackets bolt to the channels | Hollow block or weak infill walls, large cavities and tall storeys |
| Kerf rail system | The blade of a horizontal rail slides into a groove along the panel's top and bottom edges | Regular grids of equal panels and rail-based ventilated facades; stone of 30 mm and more |
| Undercut anchors | An anchor locks by shape into an undercut hole drilled in the back of the panel (not through it); a hanger on it hooks onto a horizontal rail | Thin hard stone, porcelain, large panels and facades where single panels must be replaceable |

## Engineering and specifications

| Item | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Engineering | Design is by the project engineer or consultant. Either installation to approved shop drawings supplied by the consultant or main contractor, or an independent facade engineer appointed for the project (design basis, wind loads per the current SBC 301, calculations for the steel substructure, shop drawings, part list, weekly site visits on those projects) |
| Wind load | Calculated for each project by the project engineer to the current Saudi Building Code SBC 301 |
| Panel thickness | Natural stone typically 30 mm, thicker on demand; marble and granite often 20 mm (exterior 20 mm panels on edge fixings need the engineer's check and stone tests, or an undercut system); porcelain per the panel maker's system |
| Anchors | Type and size per the engineer's calculation and the consultant's specification; site pull-out tests on request, arranged with the anchor manufacturer or a testing laboratory and witnessed by the consultant |
| Metalwork | Brackets and angles in stainless steel or hot-dip galvanised steel according to the project specification |
| Thermal movement | Each panel is held by mechanical fixings with a joint around it, so daily expansion and contraction is not passed to the next panel |
| Joints | Open or sealed, width per approved shop drawings |
| Documents for consultants | Section for architects and consultants (process, fixing systems, thickness, QA/QC, maintenance guide, glossary, guide specification 04 42 00, send drawings): https://al-swaticontracting.com/for-consultants/ ; CAD fixing details (.DWG) and a method statement on request: https://al-swaticontracting.com/technical-specs/ |

## Why mechanical fixing in Riyadh

- Heat: Riyadh summers reach 45°C. Each mechanically fixed panel moves freely on its anchors; with wet cement fixing, stone, mortar and wall expand at different rates and the mortar bond can open hollow spots behind the stone.
- Efflorescence: with no mortar behind the stone, no cement salts wash out onto the face, so there is no mortar efflorescence (white stains), which shows most on light Riyadh limestone.
- Safety: every panel is held by mechanical fixings, so none can fall from a failed mortar bond.
- Repairs: a damaged panel can be released without breaking out mortar; with undercut anchors on rails each panel is replaced on its own.

## Prices in Riyadh (2026)

Indicative ranges in SAR per square metre for supply and installation on Up-Down brackets for a villa facade, excluding 15% VAT. The final price follows a free site visit and a written quote.

| Material | SAR per m² |
| --- | --- |
| Riyadh white stone | 230-280 |
| Riyadh limestone (beige / yellow) | 290-375 |
| Granite | 265-340 |
| Travertine and marble | 505-700 |
| Large-format porcelain | 265-340 |
| Sandstone | On request |

- Other fixing systems cost more. For Riyadh white stone: about 350-410 with C-Channel rails, 485-545 with the kerf rail system and 530-590 with undercut anchors.
- Commercial towers add about 20-25 SAR per m² for safety scaffolding.
- Shop drawings are quoted separately when a project needs them.
- What moves the price: stone grade and thickness, panel size, fixing system, building height and access, and quantity.
- Online estimate (price per m², total in SAR and installation time): https://al-swaticontracting.com/stone-cladding-cost-calculator/

## How a project runs

1. Free site visit: survey of the wall line, levels and substrate (concrete, block or AAC), which decides the anchor type.
2. Written quote: material, thickness, fixing system, quantity and price.
3. Engineering: installation to approved shop drawings supplied by the consultant or main contractor, or an independent facade engineer appointed for the project (wind loads per the current SBC 301, substructure calculations, shop drawings). Material submittals and samples for the consultant's approval.
4. Mock-up and anchor pull-out tests on request.
5. Installation by AL-Swati's own teams, row by row from the bottom of each elevation, with inspection hold points for anchors, brackets, the first row and each completed elevation.
6. Handover: final inspection, snag list, records, maintenance guide and the 5-year written workmanship warranty attested by the Chamber of Commerce, issued by the contracting company.

## Service areas

All of Riyadh, including Al Malqa, Al Narjis, Hittin, Al Yasmin, Diriyah and Al Olaya. Outside Riyadh: Dammam and Al-Ahsa.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who installs stone cladding in Riyadh with mechanical fixing?
AL-Swati Contracting, a Riyadh contractor with experience since 1994, installs natural stone, marble, granite and porcelain facades with mechanical fixing, using its own direct workforce, with a 5-year written workmanship warranty attested by the Chamber of Commerce, issued by the contracting company.

### How much does stone cladding cost in Riyadh in 2026?
Supply and installation on Up-Down brackets for a villa facade costs about 230-280 SAR/m² for Riyadh white stone, 290-375 for beige or yellow Riyadh limestone, 265-340 for granite or large-format porcelain and 505-700 for travertine or marble, excluding 15% VAT.

### What stone thickness is used on mechanically fixed facades?
Natural stone is typically 30 mm, thicker on demand. Marble and granite are often 20 mm; exterior 20 mm panels on edge fixings need the engineer's check and stone tests, or an undercut system. Porcelain thickness follows the panel maker's system.

### How is wind load designed?
The project engineer calculates the wind load for each project to the current Saudi Building Code SBC 301. AL-Swati installs to approved shop drawings supplied by the consultant or main contractor, or appoints an independent facade engineer for the project.

### Which fixing systems does AL-Swati install?
Up-Down angle brackets, PEN pin fixing, vertical C-Channel rails, kerf rails and undercut anchors. Brackets are stainless or hot-dip galvanised steel according to the project specification. AL-Swati can install systems from Hilti, fischer and Rockany.

### Which manufacturers' systems does AL-Swati install?
AL-Swati installs fixing systems from Hilti, fischer and Rockany, and local or imported accessories, as the project specification names. Product approvals belong to the manufacturer and are submitted with the material submittal. Undercut experience: Hilti undercut anchors on 30 mm natural stone and on 20 mm porcelain.

### Is mechanical fixing better than cement for Riyadh's heat?
Mechanical fixing lets each panel move with the heat on its own fixings, leaves no mortar behind the stone to cause mortar efflorescence, and keeps every panel held by mechanical fixings. Wet cement fixing depends on a mortar bond that heat cycles can weaken.

### Does AL-Swati work outside Riyadh?
Yes. AL-Swati works across Riyadh and also in Dammam and Al-Ahsa.

### How do I get a quote?
Call or WhatsApp +966 51 182 6313, email info@al-swaticontracting.com, or use the form at https://al-swaticontracting.com/contact/. The site visit is free and the quote is written.

## ملخص بالعربية

شركة السواتي للمقاولات مقاول تركيب حجر في الرياض له أكثر من 500 مشروع من الخبرة منذ 1994 بين فلل وأبراج ومبانٍ تجارية. تركّب الشركة واجهات الحجر الطبيعي (حجر الرياض الأبيض والحجر الجيري البيج والأصفر والحجر الرملي والجرانيت) والرخام والبورسلان بمقاسات كبيرة، بالتثبيت الميكانيكي فقط، وبفريق عمل مباشر من الشركة دون مقاولين من الباطن.

- أنظمة التثبيت: زوايا Up-Down، وتثبيت PEN بالدبابيس، ومجاري C-Channel الرأسية، ونظام Kerf، ومراسي Undercut. الزوايا من الستانلس ستيل أو الحديد المجلفن على الساخن حسب مواصفة المشروع، ومقاسات الانكرات والبراغي حسب حساب المهندس ومواصفة الاستشاري.
- الأعمال الهندسية: تنفّذ الشركة حسب مخططات تنفيذية معتمدة من الاستشاري أو المقاول الرئيسي، أو تعيّن مهندس واجهات مستقلاً للمشروع يُعدّ أحمال الرياح حسب كود البناء السعودي SBC 301 الساري وحسابات الهيكل المعدني والمخططات التنفيذية.
- طلبات اعتماد المواد والعينات، ونموذج تجريبي واختبارات سحب للانكرات عند الطلب، وضمان مكتوب على التنفيذ لمدة 5 سنوات، مصدّق من الغرفة التجارية، تصدره شركة المقاولات.
- قسم المعماريين والاستشاريين: https://al-swaticontracting.com/ar/for-consultants/
- أسعار 2026 للتوريد والتركيب على زوايا Up-Down لواجهة فيلا، بالريال للمتر المربع ودون ضريبة القيمة المضافة: حجر الرياض الأبيض 230-280، الحجر الجيري البيج أو الأصفر 290-375، الجرانيت 265-340، الترافرتين والرخام 505-700، البورسلان بمقاسات كبيرة 265-340.
- مناطق العمل: جميع أحياء الرياض ومنها الملقا والنرجس وحطين والياسمين والدرعية والعليا، إضافة إلى الدمام والأحساء.
